dimensions.note: One new secret leaves the extension: the owner's personal access token or machine key JSON from instanceCreate, in InstanceOwnerCredential.secret, marked sensitive, so swamp vaults it; batch Q read the record back from disk and found a vault.get reference, not the token. It is written before any further call, since a new instance is not readable the moment it is created (the first live run hit HTTP 404 on the read-back and would have lost the token; the read-back is gone). A human owner is refused by design: it would need a password in the request. EmailProvider stores sender, host and the SMTP login name, never the password or an HTTP signing key; batch Q made a provider with a marker password and asserted the marker is in no stored artifact. InstanceMember, TrustedDomain, InstanceInfo and AuthSummary carry no secret. The instance type and the settings reads need iam.read, iam.member.read or iam.write and say so, so a reader key is refused by Zitadel (batch Q: a reader cannot trust a domain), not helped past.

instanceCreate logs the name, the owner's username and the credential kind at info and the created id at warning, never the body or the secret; trustedDomainRemove logs at warning. authFactorList logs how many people and factors; the settings 403 warning names all four v1 Admin reads it now covers. No key, token, PAT or provider password reaches a log line; the first smoke run's failure message carried the instance id and Zitadel's own text only.

instanceCreate fails before writing anything when Zitadel names no instance id or returns no pat or key, unit tested; a missing expirationDate is refused by the schema before any call (batch Q). domainList, domainAdd, domainRemove and domainSetPrimary still refuse to guess between two instances and name them (batch Q, live, after the second instance existed); the reachable check no longer requires exactly one instance, since a definition used for instanceList or instanceCreate has none to name, unit tested with two. trustedDomainRemove refuses a domain that is not trusted and a confirm that does not match, both before the DELETE. In settings read only an HTTP 403 on the v1 Admin block is downgraded to a warning, as before; the email and notification reads sit inside that block, so a reader of one organization is told once. A Zitadel older than the /admin/v1/email service would answer 404 and fail the read; v4 is what the suite runs and the README names.

133 unit tests, 13 new: instanceList with two instances; instanceCreate unchanged on a present name with one call and nothing minted, the full body sent for a pat owner with the secret stored first, the key JSON decoded from base64, the refusal when no credential comes back, and the reachable check over two instances with a throwaway RSA key; the instance type's read, memberList, trustedDomainAdd twice, and trustedDomainRemove through present, confirm, dryRun and the DELETE with the tombstone; settings read storing the email provider without a password and the notification record, and both absent under 403; authFactorList with a summary for one person, and the fan-out over two humans with one of them not ready. Live: the whole smoke suite on a throwaway Zitadel v4.19.3 in podman from this checkout, 260 checks over fixtures and batches a to q, all passing; the new batch Q is 31 of them and found two defects on its first run that are fixed here (the read-back 404 and the preflight over two instances).

instanceCreate converges on the name: a second run lists, finds, stores unchanged and makes no call to _create (batch Q live, unit tested). trustedDomainAdd lists first and reports unchanged. domainSetPrimary on the custom domain a creation named is unchanged, since Zitadel makes that domain primary at creation; the argument's description says so now. The residual risk is a run interrupted between the POST to _create and the first writeResource: the instance exists, its owner's credential was returned once and is gone, and the next run reports unchanged. The window is one in-memory write with no network call in it, and the only recovery is Zitadel's own RemoveInstance and a new create, which this type does not do on purpose.

Paths and bodies read from proto/zitadel/system.proto, admin.proto, instance.proto, member.proto, settings.proto and policy.proto at main and confirmed live on v4.19.3: POST /system/v1/instances/_search and _create (instanceName, firstOrgName, customDomain, defaultLanguage, machine.personalAccessToken or machine.machineKey of KEY_TYPE_JSON, answering instanceId, pat or machineKey as base64); GET /admin/v1/instances/me; POST /admin/v1/domains/_search, /trusted_domains/_search and /members/_search, all paged with searchAll; POST /admin/v1/trusted_domains and DELETE /admin/v1/trusted_domains/{domain}; POST /admin/v1/email/_search and GET /admin/v1/policies/notification. GetMyInstance, ListInstanceDomains and the trusted-domain rpcs are marked deprecated at main in favour of the v2 instance service, which is beta and absent on the versions deployed; the paths answer on v4.19.3 and the module doc names the API. The System API lists instances with limit 1000 and no paging, as before.

No new long-lived handles, timers or caches. authFactorList without a user makes two calls per human after one paged user search; an organization with a thousand people is two thousand calls in one run, which is the fan-out rule 6 asks for rather than a thousand runs.

README: a new instance section, the system section rewritten for six methods with why the owner is a machine user and why there is no instanceRemove, the settings and user paragraphs, and the Which API paragraph. Manifest: nine types, the new records and methods, instance.ts in models, an instances label. The smoke README documents mksystem.sh and batch Q. Example values are .invalid and example.org names; the one password in the tree is the marker mksmtp.ts gives a provider on a throwaway, which batch Q asserts is never stored. The .review report is committed with the release as before.

InstanceCreateArgs: name min 1, ownerCredential a z.enum of two with a default, ownerUsername defaulting to admin, expirationDate a non-empty string that Zitadel validates as RFC3339; the schema refusal is live tested. AuthFactorListArgs.user is optional and min 1 when given. InstanceOwnerCredential has every field required but none optional beyond what the API may omit; InstanceMember.roles is an array; AuthSummary counts are numbers and the flags booleans. EmailProvider makes the SMTP fields optional since an HTTP provider has none.

instance-owner is infinite with garbageCollection 5, as the other emitted-once secret specs; instance 5; instance-domain, trusted-domain, member, email-provider, notification and auth-summary infinite with 10, as every other list record. Fixed names, so repeated reads overwrite rather than accumulate; trustedDomainRemove tombstones the one instance it removed, kind action.

Instances: list and create here, update and remove not, on purpose — removing an instance removes every organization and user in it and stays a deliberate act with the key in hand; the README says so. Trusted domains: list in read, add, remove; the Admin API has no update. Members: read only; adding a member is AddIAMMember, left out as the org type leaves out organization membership. Email providers and the notification policy: read only, as every other settings kind the type does not write.

The shared checks run before every method of the instance type. The system type's reachable check now signs the assertion and lists instances, passing with any count, so a multi-instance deployment can run instanceList and instanceCreate; the domain methods resolve the instance when they run and refuse with the ids when there are several. Unit tested, and live: batch Q ran instanceCreate and instanceList after the second instance existed.

instance-<id>, as domainList already named it, because an instance's name is mutable through UpdateInstance and two instances may be named alike; instance-owner-<instanceName>-<ownerUsername>; trusted-domain-<domain>; member-<preferredLoginName> falling back to the user id, through the sanitiser so an @ becomes a dash (member-kari-example-org, unit tested); email-provider-<description> falling back to the id; notification-instance; auth-summary-<username> beside the auth-factor-<username>-<type>-<id> names read already wrote. The reads and the writes of a trusted domain use the same name, so a remove overwrites the add's record and the tombstone names it.

No method reads stored state back. instanceCreate reads the live list for the name; trustedDomainAdd and Remove read the live trusted list. A workflow asserts on data.latest of auth-summary-<username>.mfa, instance-owner-<name>-<owner>.secret is a vault reference it can pass on, and instance-<id>.instanceId feeds a definition's instanceId.

All eight existing types move to 2026.11.08.1 with an upgrade entry each: system names the two methods and the friendlier state spelling, user names the optional argument and the summary, settings the two records, the others say nothing in them changed. instance.ts is new with an empty upgrades list, which the push warns about non-blockingly and --skip-upgrade-check acknowledges. Attributes pass through unchanged: no existing argument changed its meaning. The manifest is 2026.11.08.1.
